picks.headline: Physics-informed machine learning speeds the hunt for 2D flat-band quantum materials
picks.excerpt: A University of Manchester team developed a physics-informed machine-learning method that hunts for two-dimensional 'flat-band' quantum materials, screening over 10,000 candidates with 98.2% accuracy. The approach replaces slow density-functional-theory calculations, dramatically speeding the search for exotic quantum materials.
picks.rationale: New physics-informed ML screens 10,000+ candidates at 98.2% accuracy, replacing slow DFT — a concrete method shift for quantum-materials discovery; no URL or content match in published science history.

picks.headline: Inside David Baker's Institute for Protein Design and its open 'communal brain'
picks.excerpt: A look inside David Baker's Institute for Protein Design, where a 100+ researcher lab and its open 'communal brain' of deep-learning tools (RFdiffusion and successors) now design proteins from scratch with atomic precision. The piece maps how AI-driven protein design is reshaping how biotech invents antibodies, enzymes and medicines.
picks.rationale: Insider map of David Baker's open AI protein-design toolchain (RFdiffusion et al.) reshaping how biotech invents medicines; distinct topic and outlet, credible, not previously published.

picks.headline: Open AI drug-metabolism contest ends in a 28-way tie — data quality, not model size, wins
picks.excerpt: An open AI competition to predict drug metabolism (whether compounds activate the PXR receptor that clears roughly half of all marketed drugs) ended in a 28-way statistical tie, with startup Inductive Bio narrowly on top. The result suggests data quality, not raw model size, drives performance in AI-for-drug-discovery, reshaping how the field benchmarks its models.
picks.rationale: Actionable benchmarking insight for AI-drug-discovery — an open PXR-metabolism contest ties 28 ways, showing data quality beats model scale; net-new, credible outlet, distinct topic and source.

picks.headline: GOFLOW reconstructs fine-scale ocean currents from satellite thermal imagery
picks.excerpt: Tel Aviv University researchers built GOFLOW, an AI system that reconstructs fine-scale ocean surface currents from satellite thermal imagery, revealing small-scale dynamics that standard models miss. Better maps of these currents sharpen climate, weather and ocean-atmosphere gas-exchange predictions.
picks.rationale: Newest pick (07-20): GOFLOW recovers small-scale ocean currents from thermal satellite data that standard models miss, sharpening climate and weather prediction; net-new, distinct outlet and Earth-science topic.
